{{respell|eh|PAY|_|OO|doh}};[https://www.espn.com/dallas/ncb/columns/story?columnist=caplan_jeff&id=4867681 A fresh transfusion of talent] born May 20, 1987) is a Nigerian-American{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/30/world/europe/ekpe-udoh-from-nba-washout-to-cult-hero-in-turkey.html |title=From N.B.A. Bench Player to Cult Hero in Turkey |work=New York Times |first=Patrick |last=Kingsley |date=30 June 2017}} professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is an assistant coach for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] and the [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor Bears]]. In the [[2010 NBA draft]], he was selected by the [[Golden State Warriors]] with the sixth overall pick. With a 7'4 {{frac|1|2}}" [[Wingspan#Wingspan in sports|wingspan]], Udoh was the [[Big 12 Conference]]'s leading shot blocker during the 2009–10 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Ekpe-Udoh-1220/ |title=DraftExpressProfile: Ekpe Udoh, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook |access-date=March 29, 2010 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923225319/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Ekpe-Udoh-1220/ |url-status=dead }}[https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/colleges/post/_/id/4667722/udohs-next-choice-baylor-or-nba Udoh's next choice: Baylor or NBA?] He led the conference in his only season at [[2009–10 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor (2009–10)]], after transferring from [[University of Michigan|Michigan]] where, as a sophomore for the [[2007–08 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2007–08 Michigan Wolverines]], he led the [[Big Ten Conference]] in blocked shots with 2.9 per game (92 blocks total) in 2007–08.{{Cite web |url=http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/udoh_ekpe00.html |title=Ekpe Udoh Bio |access-date=2010-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720095134/http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/udoh_ekpe00.html |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead }} A two−time [[All-EuroLeague Team]] selection, Udoh led Fenerbahçe to a [[EuroLeague]] title in [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|2017]], earning the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] award in the process. Udoh was selected for the senior [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigerian national team]] for both the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]] and the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Olympic Games]].{{cite news |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/team/Nigeria |title=Nigeria Profile|work=FIBA }} ==College career== Udoh played three seasons of college basketball, two at Michigan and one at Baylor, averaging 8.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.8 blocks per game in 103 career games. His teammate, [[Jesse Scotford]] lead the team in points, often assisted by Udoh. In 2009–10, Udoh earned honorable mention All-American honors by the Associated Press, as well as being named to the All-Big 12 second team, Big 12 All-Defensive team, Big 12 Newcomer of the Year, Big 12 All-Rookie team, USBWA All-District VII team and NABC Division I All-District 8 second team. On April 13, 2010, he declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.[https://www.espn.com/dallas/news/story?id=5082895 Baylor F Udoh declares for NBA draft] ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2010–2012)=== [[File:Ekpe Udoh.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Udoh with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2011]] Udoh was selected with the sixth overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Because of a wrist injury,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5380912|title=Udoh out 6 months following surgery|date=July 14, 2010|work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 23, 2010}} Udoh did not make his NBA debut until December 11, 2010, against the [[Miami Heat]] in the final three minutes of the game, scoring two points. ===Bnei Herzliya (2011)=== On November 21, 2011, Udoh signed with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of Israel for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/88971/ekpe-udoh-signs-in-israel-with-bnei-hasharon.html Ekpe Udoh signs in Israel with Bnei Hasharon] In December 2011, he returned to the Warriors after managing just one game for Bnei where he recorded 22 points, 16 rebounds, 3 assists and 4 blocks. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2012–2014)=== On March 13, 2012, Udoh, along with [[Monta Ellis]] and [[Kwame Brown]], was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Andrew Bogut]] and [[Stephen Jackson]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-monta-ellis-ekpe-udoh-and-kwame-brown-warriors | title=Bucks Acquire Monta Ellis, Ekpe Udoh and Kwame Brown from Warriors | work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. | date=March 13, 2012 | access-date=March 14, 2012}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2014–2015) === On September 3, 2014, Udoh signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite news|title=Clippers Sign Chris Douglas-Roberts and Ekpe Udoh|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-sign-chris-douglas-roberts-and-ekpe-udoh|access-date=September 3, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 3, 2014}} Throughout the season, he appeared in 33 games, failing to secure larger playing time and role. ===Fenerbahçe (2015–2017)=== On July 28, 2015, Udoh signed a one-year deal with the Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce adds size with Udoh|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/68e7s5x4rr4b4phj|access-date=July 28, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 28, 2015}} In his first season with the team, Udoh already had a starting role, being one of the team's leaders. Fenerbahçe won the [[Turkish Cup Basketball|Turkish Cup]], with 67–65 win over [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]]. Fenerbahçe also reached the [[EuroLeague Finals|final game]] of the [[2016 EuroLeague Final Four]], but fell short of winning the EuroLeague championship, after an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] 96–101 loss to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow claims its seventh Euroleague crown after OT thriller|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2015#!report|website=euroleague.net|access-date=9 September 2016}} Over 27 EuroLeague games, he averaged 12.6 points and 5.1 rebounds per game. At the end of the season, Fenerbahçe also won the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]] championship. On July 11, 2016, Udoh re-signed with Fenerbahçe, on a 1+1 contract.{{cite news|title=EKPE UDOH İLE ANLAŞMAYA news|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=263&seasoncode=E2016#!report|title=Fenerbahçe Istanbul is EuroLeague ===Shimane Susanoo Magic (2022–2023)=== On December 24, 2022, Udoh signed with the [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]]. ===Kyoto Hannaryz (2023)=== On February 28, 2023, he signed with the [[Kyoto Hannaryz]]. ==National team career== Udoh was a member of the senior men's [[Nigerian men's national basketball team|Nigerian national team]]. He represented Nigeria at the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]], and at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]]. ==Coaching career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2023–present)=== On June 14, 2023, Udoh was announced as an assistant coach for the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Atlanta Hawks]] under head coach [[Quin Snyder]].{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2023 |title=Atlanta Hawks Announce Coaching Staff |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-announce-coaching-staff |access-date=June 14, 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2010}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2010–11 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State]] | 58 || '''18''' || 17.8 || .437 || — || .656 || 3.1 || .7 || .4 || 1.5 || 4.1 |- | style="text-align:left;" rowspan="2"| {{nbay|2011}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2011–12 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State]] | 38 || 6 || '''21.8''' || .443 || — || .719 || 3.9 || .8 || '''.7''' || '''1.7''' || 5.5 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2011–12 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 23 || 5 || 20.1 || .409 || .000 || '''.800''' || '''4.7''' || '''1.1''' || '''.7''' || 1.6 || '''5.7''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2012}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2012–13 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | '''76''' || 9 || 17.3 || .435 || .000 || .748 || 3.3 || .6 || .5 || 1.1 || 4.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2013}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2013–14 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 42 || 14 || 19.1 || .399 || — || .638 || 3.5 || .7 || .4 || 1.0 || 3.4 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2014}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2014–15 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
